encounters.cc: Presents for routine health examination and discussion of contraception after starting a new sexual relationship.

lines: Presents for routine health examination and discussion of contraception after starting a new sexual relationship.
She reports no current symptoms but mentions that she has recently started a new sexual relationship and would like to discuss contraception and sexually transmitted infection (STI) prevention.
She has never been pregnant and has regular menstrual cycles.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago.
She inquires about the need for any testing given her new relationship.
She has no significant past medical history
Alcohol: Social use (1-2 drinks per week).
She denies any history of genital lesions, vaginal discharge, or dysuria.
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits, and
Her pelvic examination is unremarkable with no cervical motion tenderness or adnexal masses palpated.
She has a normal bimanual examination and no mucopurulent cervical discharge.

encounters.cc: Concerns about white vaginal discharge without odor, itching, or irritation present for several months.

lines: Concerns about white vaginal discharge without odor, itching, or irritation present for several months.

The patient returns to the clinic three months after her initial visit for routine health examination and contraception counseling upon starting a new sexual relationship, and presents to her primary care physician with concerns about a vaginal discharge that she has noticed for the past several months.
She reports that the discharge is white and does not have an odor.
She denies any itching, burning, or irritation.
Her last menstrual period started 14 days ago, and she has regular 28-day cycles.
The patient is sexually active with one partner and uses condoms inconsistently.
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits.
Pelvic examination reveals a small amount of white mucoid discharge in the cervical os.
There is no erythema, lesions, or signs of trauma.
A sample of the discharge is obtained for microscopic examination, which shows:

encounters.cc: Two-week history of fever, malaise, and rash spreading from trunk to extremities including palms and soles; reports painless genital ulcers that resolved several months ago.

lines: Two-week history of fever, malaise, and rash spreading from trunk to extremities including palms and soles; reports painless genital ulcers that resolved several months ago.
The patient presents to the emergency department approximately 18 months following a negative syphilis screening during routine gynecologic care and subsequent evaluation for vaginal discharge.
She reports that the rash began on her trunk and has since spread to her extremities, including the palms of her hands and the soles of her feet.
She also mentions that she has noticed several painless ulcers in her genital area that appeared a few months ago but then resolved on their own.
She has not sought medical attention for these symptoms until now.
She is not currently on any medications
She is sexually active with multiple partners and does not consistently use condoms.
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, you note a diffuse, non-itchy maculopapular rash and generalized lymphadenopathy, including palpable epitrochlear nodes.
Laboratory tests are ordered, and the results are as follows:
- Rapid plasma reagin (RPR): Positive at a 1:64 dilution
- Treponema pallidum particle agglutination assay (TP-PA): Positive

encounters.cc: Three-day history of dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and yellow vaginal discharge without fever or back pain.

lines: Three-day history of dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and yellow vaginal discharge without fever or back pain.

This 25-year-old female with history of prior emergency evaluation for genital lesions and previous gynecologic assessments presents to the clinic with a 3-day history of dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and a yellow vaginal discharge.
She reports no fever, back pain, or abdominal pain.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago and was normal.
She is sexually active with multiple partners and inconsistently uses condoms.
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits.
Pelvic examination reveals mucopurulent cervical discharge and cervical motion tenderness.
Urinalysis shows no signs of bacteria or white blood cells.

encounters.cc: Painful urination and genital lesions for three days with flu-like symptoms including fever and malaise one week after unprotected intercourse.

lines: Painful urination and genital lesions for three days with flu-like symptoms including fever and malaise one week after unprotected intercourse.
The patient with prior syphilis and chlamydia presents to the ED.
She reports the onset of flu-like symptoms, including fever and malaise, one week after having unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner.
Alcohol: Social use (1-2 drinks per week).
On examination, you note multiple small vesicles and ulcers on the labia, as well as bilateral tender inguinal lymphadenopathy.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of migratory multiple joint pains and swelling associated with fever and vesiculopustular rash on extremities.

lines: Two-day history of migratory multiple joint pains and swelling associated with fever and vesiculopustular rash on extremities.
The patient returns to the emergency department with a known history of prior sexually transmitted infections including early syphilis, chlamydial cervicitis, and primary genital herpes.
She reports that the pain migrates from one joint to another and is associated with fever and chills.
She also mentions a new rash that started as small red spots on her extremities and has progressed to vesiculopustular lesions.
- Primary genital herpes simplex virus infection (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
She is sexually active with multiple partners and does not consistently use barrier protection.
On examination, her temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), heart rate is 102/min, and blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg.
Physical examination reveals a young woman in moderate distress due to pain.
There is noticeable swelling and tenderness of the wrists and knees with evidence of tenosynovitis.
Several small vesiculopustular lesions are noted on her extremities, some with surrounding erythema.
- Gram stain of skin lesion exudate: Gram-negative diplococci
Based on the patient's presentation and test results,

encounters.cc: Three-day history of fever and migratory joint pains affecting knees, wrists, and ankles with associated swelling and severe tenderness.

lines: Three-day history of fever and migratory joint pains affecting knees, wrists, and ankles with associated swelling and severe tenderness.
Patient returns with symptoms similar to her January 2024 presentation, with a history of syphilis, chlamydia, and HSV.
She reports migratory joint pains affecting her knees, wrists, and ankles with swelling and severe tenderness, and a new rash on her extremities.
- Primary genital herpes simplex virus infection (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
She is sexually active with multiple partners and does not consistently use condoms.
On examination, her temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), heart rate is 102 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg
Physical examination reveals a petechial rash on her palms and soles, and her right knee is erythematous, warm, and swollen with a decreased range of motion due to pain.
There is also evidence of tenosynovitis in her wrists.
Synovial fluid analysis from her right knee shows:
Blood cultures are obtained, and a nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) from cervical and pharyngeal swabs is performed.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of severe pain and swelling in right knee with low-grade fever and painless pustules on palm.

lines: Two-day history of severe pain and swelling in right knee with low-grade fever and painless pustules on palm.
This 29-year-old female with a history of disseminated gonococcal infections in 2024 and 2025 presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of severe pain and swelling in her right knee.
She denies any recent trauma or injury to the knee.
She also reports a low-grade fever and a few small, painless pustules on her palm.
- Primary genital herpes simplex virus infection (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
She is sexually active with multiple partners and does not consistently use condoms.
She denies any vaginal discharge or pain.
Her vital signs are as follows: temperature 38.2°C, blood pressure 120/75 mmHg, heart rate 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute.
On physical examination, her right knee is warm, swollen, and tender to palpation.
There is a limited range of motion due to pain.
The skin over her palms shows a few scattered pustules with an erythematous base.
Arthrocentesis of the right knee is performed, revealing a white blood cell count of 20,000/mm³ with 90% neutrophils.
Gram stain shows no organisms, and cultures are pending.
